raw_response:
I've been farming these 13 mu for 40 years now. I'm 62, my back isn't what it used to be, but I still know every inch of this land. My son works in the county town at a construction site, and my daughter-in-law helps me and my wife when she's not looking after the little ones. So for the farm work, it's mostly the three of us old folks, plus my son comes back for harvest if he can get time off.

This year, like every year, my main land is the 8 mu where I do wheat and maize back-to-back. The wheat went in last October around the 10th — I used my own saved seed, good clean seed that I treated with medicine myself. Before planting I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer for every 2 mu, that's my usual. The wheat came up well and overwintered fine. Now it's April, the wheat is greening up. I'll give it one more watering at jointing time — probably in another week or so if it doesn't rain — and topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu. Old Wang from the east side of the village tried cutting back on fertilizer last year to save money, and his wheat was noticeably shorter. I'm not making that mistake. I'll irrigate three times total for the wheat: green-up, jointing, and filling. The electricity for the pump costs me, but you can't skip it. Wheat harvest will be around early June, I'll hire the combine — 50 yuan per mu, done in half a day.

Then the rush starts — maize has to go in within 3-4 days after wheat harvest, sometimes less if the weather turns. I buy hybrid maize seed from the dealer in town, about 50 yuan per mu. I plant it right into the wheat stubble, no time for plowing. At planting I put down compound fertilizer, about one bag per 2 mu, same as wheat. Then when the maize gets to big喇叭口 stage, I'll add some urea — about 15-20 kg per mu depending on how it looks. If the leaves are dark green and growing well, maybe I skip the topdress and save a little. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat, usually twice is enough if the summer rains cooperate. I expect about 500 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

I keep 3 mu for cotton. Cotton is a lot of hand work — planting, thinning, weeding, and picking three or four times. My daughter-in-law is good with the cotton, she has patient hands. I plant in late April, use hybrid seed. Cotton fertilizer is about 15 kg of compound per mu at planting, then another 10 kg of urea when it flowers. I irrigate twice — once at flowering, once at boll stage. For pesticides, I spray for weeds right after planting, and for bollworm I watch carefully — if I see eggs, I spray immediately, usually 2-3 times total. Cotton prices have been decent lately, so I keep at it, but honestly if my daughter-in-law didn't help, I'd think about giving it up — too much bending and picking for an old man.

The remaining 2 mu or so near the house I plant with mungbean. It's not much, but the beans are good for family eating — porridge in summer — and the stalks feed our goats. I put a little fertilizer, maybe 10 kg compound per mu at planting, and after that I mostly leave it alone. No irrigation, just rain. Low work, low cost.

Money is always tight. Seven people in the household, and my son's wages don't always come on time from those construction bosses. I'll spend maybe 3,600 yuan on inputs this year. I could spend more on fertilizer and maybe get a bit more yield, but then what if someone gets sick? I need to keep 2,000 yuan in my pocket for emergencies. Better to be a little safe than sorry. That's how I've survived 40 years of farming.
